hero.lead: A nation of 14.4 million on the shore of the second-largest freshwater lake on Earth by volume, where one citizen in five has electricity.

capital.heading: 19 instruments. Hydropower, clean water, a railway, health and human capital, and a new private power utility.

register.name: Burundi Integrated Community Development Project, 2026 financing
register.detail: Approved 30 September 2026 · World Bank Finances One · First approved February 2020 at $60 million
register.note: Nutrition, basic services and economic opportunity
register.text: World Bank financing for the Integrated Community Development Project, whose objective is to improve nutrition, access to basic services and economic opportunities in its target areas, among them communes that host refugee camps. The project was first approved in February 2020 for $60 million. It bears on food, health and livelihood.

register.name: Solar Energy in Local Communities (SOLEIL-Nyakiriza), 2026 financing
register.detail: Approved 4 September 2026 · World Bank Finances One
register.text: World Bank financing for the national project that brings solar power to local communities, known as SOLEIL-Nyakiriza. The ASCENT Burundi programme was designed to complement it. It bears on the energy standard.

register.name: Water Supply and Sanitation Access Project (PAEPA)
register.detail: Approved 10 December 2025 · IDA grant · Government adds $10 million
register.text: A new treatment plant adds 60,000 m³ of water a day to Bujumbura. Clean water for 615,000 people, about 490,000 of them piped at home, and basic sanitation for 55,000 people in rural areas: the Bank’s first water and sanitation operation in Burundi in more than 15 years.

register.name: Burundi Colline Climate Resilience Project (NAGURA)
register.detail: Announced 19 December 2024 · IDA $70 million · Global Environment Facility $18.3 million
register.note: $88.3 million in all, with the GEF
register.text: Restores degraded land and builds climate resilience in 80 collines across 87 sub-watersheds, reaching 1.3 million people and 213,320 households directly. It is expected to bring work to 309,680 residents, 40% of them young people and 51% women, and 42,000 indirect jobs.

register.name: MIGA guarantee for Weza Power
register.detail: Issued 19 December 2024 · Breach of contract cover · Up to three years
register.note: Covers the feasibility phase for now
register.text: Covers Anzana Electric Group’s investment in Weza Power against breach of the project agreement. Weza Power is a new private utility in a public-private partnership to extend electricity distribution and rural electrification, the energy standard. In December 2025 MIGA disclosed a proposed amendment extending the cover to the construction of Lot 3 (Poste Sud–Ijenda), expected to connect about 10,400 new customers.

register.name: Human Capital Development Project
register.detail: Announced 30 July 2024 · IDA grant · $27.6 million from the Global Partnership for Education
register.note: $227.6 million in all, a record for Burundi
register.text: One project for nutrition, health care and basic education, with early childhood development, health teams in schools and performance-based financing in education. It is expected to reach an estimated 13.2 million people over five years, including 1.9 million refugees and members of host communities.

register.name: Burundi Urban Resilience Emergency Project (IBISAGARA BIRAMA)
register.detail: Announced 1 July 2024 · $60 million IDA grant · $53 million from the Crisis Response Window Plus
register.text: Emergency flood response, flood defences, early warning and risk-informed land-use plans for Bujumbura, where more than 200,000 people were directly affected by the flood emergency. It also protects key water-supply infrastructure.

register.name: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation (ASCENT Burundi)
register.detail: Announced 26 June 2024 · IDA grant · $90 million more from AFD, the European Union and the EIB
register.text: Supports the Government’s Universal Access Program: the medium-voltage network, Bujumbura’s distribution network, and a distribution pilot led by Weza Power, the new private utility. It aims to bring electricity to about 2.4 million people, 1,200 public institutions and 6,000 small and medium enterprises.

register.name: Access to Finance to Import Strategic Commodities (AFISC)
register.detail: Announced 10 January 2024 · IDA grant · Two-year trade facility at the central bank
register.text: Backs commercial banks’ letters of credit for imports of fertilizer and pharmaceuticals while the currency is liberalised, through the Banque de la République du Burundi. About 2 million smallholder farmers are expected to benefit from the fertilizer.

register.name: Burundi Jobs and Economic Transformation Project (JET)
register.detail: Announced 1 December 2023 · IDA grant · Five years
register.note: Credit and markets for small firms
register.text: Makes credit easier, cheaper and more secure for micro, small and medium enterprises, through credit infrastructure, bank guarantee products and digital financial services, and supports the reforms and equipment firms need. It aims at 4,228 direct and 113,000 indirect jobs, with a focus on firms owned by women and refugees.

register.name: Burundi Transport Resilience Project
register.detail: Announced 6 October 2022 · IDA financing · Five years
register.note: National Road 3, the corridor to Tanzania
register.text: Makes the main road corridor from Burundi to Tanzania, National Road 3, efficient, safe and climate resilient, with social infrastructure for the communities along it in Bujumbura, Kabezi and Muhuta. It also builds road management capacity and trains future transport specialists, with a focus on bringing more women into the sector.

register.name: Cash for Jobs Project (Merankabandi)
register.detail: Announced 14 December 2021 · IDA grant · All 18 provinces · Closing 31 December 2027
register.note: Plus $50 million of additional financing, $200 million in all
register.text: Cash transfers, measures that lead to jobs, stronger social protection systems and the inclusion of refugees, across all 18 provinces. The World Bank reports that the national programme has reached over 1.5 million people with cash transfers, startup capital and crisis response.

register.name: Jiji and Mulembwe Hydropower
register.detail: Approved 22 April 2014 · IDA grants of $100 million (2014) and $50 million (2024) · Jiji inaugurated June 2025, Mulembwe June 2026
register.note: Plus a $33.1 million EU trust fund grant
register.text: Two hydropower plants in the south of the country, 32.5 MW at Jiji and 17 MW at Mulembwe, producing about 239 GWh a year together; the African Development Bank says they will help nearly double national generation capacity. Clean power for a grid that reaches one citizen in five.

register.name: Water Sector and Climate Resilience Building Support Programme (PASEREC), Phase 1
register.detail: Additional grant announced 24 October 2025 · African Development Fund, Climate Action Window · To 2029
register.text: Safe drinking water for about 500,000 people in Bubanza, Cibitoke, Cankuzo, Rutana and Ruyigi, with 17 solar-powered water systems, eco-friendly sanitation and irrigation. About 2,700 jobs, 80% of them for young people and women.

register.name: SEFA project preparation grant to Weza Power
register.detail: Announced 5 June 2025 · Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa
register.text: Speeds the preparation of Weza Power, the public-private utility planned to extend electricity across Burundi, including its environmental and social work before full operations begin.

register.name: Tanzania–Burundi standard gauge railway, Phase II
register.detail: Announced 13 December 2023 · African Development Bank Group grants to Burundi · Malagarasi–Musongati section, 84 km
register.note: Burundi’s share of $696.41 million for Burundi and Tanzania
register.text: Phase II of the joint Tanzania–Burundi–DR Congo standard gauge railway: a single electrified track, with the Bank Group’s financing of $696.41 million covering 651 km on the Tanzania–Burundi line. Burundi receives $98.62 million in grants for its 84 km section; Tanzania receives loans and guarantees. A rail link to the region’s markets bears on livelihood.

register.name: U.S.–Burundi health cooperation memorandum of understanding
register.detail: Signed 6 February 2026 · Five years · More than $129 million from the United States · $26 million more from Burundi
register.text: Health assistance from the United States for HIV/AIDS, malaria and infectious disease surveillance and response: laboratory commodities, frontline health workers, data systems, malaria prevention and treatment, HIV tests and antiretroviral treatment. Burundi raises its own health spending by $26 million over the same five years.

register.name: Technical assistance grant to Weza Power
register.text: Funds a pilot to connect more than 40,000 new households and businesses from 2025, and the preparation of a national network expansion under the public-private partnership.

register.name: Songa Energy hydropower: Upper Ruvyironza and Upper Mulembwe
register.detail: Announced 11 February 2025 · Long-term project finance debt · ATIDI political risk cover
register.note: 10.65 MW in two small hydropower plants
register.text: Project finance for two run-of-the-river plants in south-central Burundi, 1.65 MW and 9.0 MW, expected on the grid in 2025 and 2027. Private power for a grid that reaches one citizen in five.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Three in four live in the countryside. Remittances equal 8.1% of GDP.

items.name: One Acre Fund (Tubura)
items.text: Working in Burundi as Tubura since 2011: seed and fertilizer on credit, training from field officers and tree seedlings for smallholders; it reports 383,000 farmers served.

items.name: Interbank Burundi
items.text: A Burundian bank that built a product, a credit scorecard and staff training for micro, small and medium enterprises with IFC advice from 2022 to 2023; IFC reports 1,102 micro loans outstanding.
